explanation: Maintain the unvisited top, bottom, left, and right boundaries. Consume each outside edge in clockwise order, checking boundaries before the final two edges.
timeComplexity: O(rows times columns) time. Each entry belongs to exactly one consumed boundary and is emitted once.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space excluding output. Four boundaries and loop indices suffice; the result stores rows times columns values.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 Java algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: The four boundaries enclose exactly the unvisited rectangle. Reading one outside edge visits each of its cells once, then moving that boundary inward removes exactly those visited cells. Guarding the final bottom and left edges prevents revisiting a single remaining row or column.
walkthrough: For [[2,4,6],[8,10,12]], read the top edge 2,4,6, then the right edge 12. The remaining bottom edge contributes 10,8 from right to left. Return [2,4,6,12,10,8].
edgeCases: Rectangular matrices need not be square.
A single row is emitted once from left to right.
A single column is emitted once from top to bottom.
